lessons.title: Seatbelt and rollover protection basics
lessons.summary: Why the seatbelt and ROPS work together, and when to buckle up.

steps.speak: The rollover protective structure only protects you if you stay inside it, and the seatbelt is what keeps you there.
Fasten the belt before you start the engine, and keep it fastened whenever the engine runs, including while you wait.
Never unbuckle to lean out or reach for something while the machine can move. Stop, lower the attachment and park first.
If the machine starts to tip, stay in the seat, hold on and brace. Do not try to jump.
There is a short captioned video of these points on your screen. Report a damaged or missing belt before operating.

questions.prompt: When should the seatbelt be fastened?

choices.text: Only when driving on the haul road
Before starting the engine and whenever it runs
Only when the supervisor is watching

questions.remediation: Fasten it before you start the engine and keep it fastened while the engine runs, even while waiting.

questions.prompt: The machine starts to tip. What do you do?

choices.text: Stay in the seat, hold on and brace

questions.remediation: Stay in the seat, belted, hold on and brace; the protective structure only works if you stay inside it.

questions.prompt: You need to reach something outside the cab. What first?

choices.text: Stop, lower the attachment and park
Ask the spotter to hold the machine

questions.remediation: Stop, lower the attachment and park before you unbuckle.

lessons.title: Pre-start walkaround inspection
lessons.summary: A step-by-step walkaround before starting heavy equipment.

steps.speak: Walk all the way around the machine before you climb in, looking at the ground as well as the machine.
Look for leaks, damaged hoses, loose guards and anything under or near the tracks or wheels.
Check lights, mirrors and the steps and handholds you will use to climb in. Report anything you find before starting.

questions.prompt: When do you do the walkaround?

choices.text: At the end of the shift only

questions.remediation: The walkaround happens before you climb in and start the machine.

questions.prompt: You find a leaking hose. What now?
questions.remediation: Report a defect before you operate.

lessons.title: Responding to a hydraulic leak
lessons.summary: How to stop safely, isolate the machine and report a hydraulic leak.

steps.speak: If you see or smell a hydraulic leak, stop in a safe place and lower attachments to the ground.
Shut the engine down and keep hands away from pinholes: fluid under pressure can pierce skin.
Report the leak with where and when it happened. You can tell me: log an incident.

questions.prompt: What is the danger of feeling for a pinhole leak with your hand?

choices.text: Fluid under pressure can pierce the skin
None, it is the fastest check

questions.remediation: Never feel for leaks by hand: pressurised fluid can pierce the skin.

questions.prompt: First thing to do when you notice a leak?

choices.text: Keep working to finish the load

questions.remediation: Stop in a safe place and lower attachments first.

lessons.title: Efficient idling and fuel use
lessons.summary: When to shut down, and how idling inside a work cycle wastes fuel.

steps.speak: An idling engine still burns fuel and adds engine hours without moving any material.
If you expect to wait more than a few minutes, tell me why, or shut down when the site rules allow it.
Inside the work cycle, avoid holding high revs while you wait for a truck; smooth, planned cycles use less fuel per load.

questions.prompt: Does an idling engine use fuel?

choices.text: Yes, it burns fuel and adds engine hours

questions.remediation: Idling burns fuel and adds engine hours without doing work.

questions.prompt: You'll wait a long time for a truck. What is best?

choices.text: Hold high revs so you are ready
Say why you're waiting, or shut down if the site allows

questions.remediation: Tell me why you're waiting, or shut down when the site allows it; don't hold revs.
Smooth, planned cycles use less fuel for each load.

lessons.title: Working-condition awareness
lessons.summary: Reading wind, rain, heat and visibility before and during outdoor work.

steps.speak: Before an outdoor task, I check wind, gusts, rain, heat and visibility against the site's limits. Listen for my findings.
Strong gusts matter most for raised loads and demolition. Keep loads low, and stop lifting when told to.
Rain softens ground and slopes. Low visibility means lights on, slower speeds and confirming your spotter.
If I can't get the weather, I say so. Unknown is not the same as safe: look for yourself.

questions.prompt: Weather is unavailable. What does that mean?
questions.remediation: Unknown weather is not safe weather: check for yourself.

questions.prompt: Which work is most affected by strong gusts?
questions.remediation: Gusts matter most for raised loads and demolition.

questions.prompt: Visibility drops to a few hundred metres. What changes?

choices.text: Lights on, slower, confirm your spotter

questions.remediation: In low visibility use lights, slow down and confirm your spotter.

lessons.title: Blind spots and people near the machine
lessons.summary: Coaching after proximity warnings: blind spots, swing areas and stopping.

steps.speak: People near the machine are hardest to see behind you and inside the swing area.
When I warn about someone close, slow down and find them. On a danger warning, stop all movement.
If I lose track of someone, that does not mean they've gone. Look around before you move.

questions.prompt: I give a danger warning for a person. What do you do?

choices.text: Sound the horn and keep going

questions.remediation: On a danger warning, stop all movement first.

questions.prompt: The warning ends because I lost the detection. Is the person gone?
questions.remediation: A lost detection is not proof: look around before moving.

questions.prompt: Where is a person hardest to see?

choices.text: Right in front of the cab
Behind the machine and in the swing area

questions.remediation: Behind the machine and inside the swing area are the blind spots.

lessons.title: Smooth control and slopes
lessons.summary: Coaching after sudden starts, sudden stops and steep-slope warnings.

steps.speak: Sudden starts and stops shake loads loose and wear the machine. Pull away and brake smoothly unless you are avoiding a hazard.
On slopes, work up and down the face rather than across it, and keep the attachment low.
If I warn about a steep slope, reduce the angle or choose another route. Your machine's manual gives its real limits.

questions.prompt: When is a hard stop the right choice?
questions.remediation: Brake smoothly; hard stops are for avoiding a hazard.

questions.prompt: How should you work a steep face?
questions.remediation: Work up and down the face with the attachment low.

questions.prompt: Where are your machine's real slope limits?

choices.text: In the Operation and Maintenance Manual

questions.remediation: Real limits come from the machine's manual; the demo settings are only assumptions.

lessons.title: Practice: someone walks behind you
lessons.summary: A short branching practice scenario about a person entering the blind spot.

steps.speak: This is a short practice scenario. Choose what you would do at each point.

nodes.prompt: You are reversing to the stockpile. I warn: caution, a person 9 metres behind the machine. What do you do?

options.text: Slow down and locate the person
options.feedback: Good: slow down and find them.

options.text: Keep reversing and sound the horn
options.feedback: The horn does not stop the machine. Slow down and find them first.

nodes.prompt: The warning becomes danger: the person is 4 metres behind. What now?

options.text: Stop all movement and make eye contact
options.feedback: Right: stop, then make eye contact.

options.text: Reverse faster to clear the area
options.feedback: Never speed up: stop all movement.

nodes.prompt: Then I say I've lost track of the person. Can you move off?

options.text: Look around first; lost is not gone
options.feedback: Correct: a lost detection is not proof they left.
A lost detection is not proof: look around first.

levels.note: Educational progression in this demo only. Not equipment certification, and separate from the dataset operator_skill. Reading text, playing media, being assigned or answering confidently never counts: only completed lessons (all steps + a passed assessment) and passed scenarios do.

retake_policy: A failed attempt never completes the lesson. The operator may start a new attempt at any time; every attempt is pinned to the lesson version it started on and kept.
defer_policy: Deferring an episode-linked lesson postpones its coaching prompt by 30 minutes of observation time. Coaching prompts are only announced while the machine is off or idle and no warning is active (urgent alerts first).
